mainTopic: The calendar from יציאת מצרים to מתן תורה: was ראש חודש סיון on Sunday (רבי יוסי) or Monday (רבנן)? A series of challenges come from ברייתות and פסוקים.
overview: Background: everyone agrees the תורה was given on שבת. רבנן say it was the 6th of סיון, so ראש חודש סיון was a Monday. רבי יוסי says it was the 7th, so ראש חודש סיון was a Sunday. The amud opens by finishing a side dispute between רבא and רב אחא בר יעקב about counting from רפידים, which depends on whether תחומין were commanded at מרה. Then the גמרא brings a ברייתא with Exodus dates that puts ראש חודש סיון on Sunday. רבנן answer that אייר had 30 days that year. When a second ברייתא says outright that אייר was short, the גמרא answers that it follows רבי יוסי. רב פפא proves from the מן story that the 15th of אייר was שבת, and רבנן again answer that אייר was lengthened. Finally, רב חביבי uses the day the משכן was set up (a Sunday) and the four-day rule of אחרים to put ראש חודש סיון on שבת, which is hard for both views. The גמרא begins answering that for רבי יוסי the year had seven short months, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Counting from the camping or from the journey
steps.stepSummary: רבא counts 'the sixth day' from when the Jews camped at סיני. רב אחא בר יעקב counts it from when they set out from רפידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבא said: the sixth day is counted] from their camping. רב אחא בר יעקב said: from their journey.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence: the word 'לחנייתן' finishes רבא's statement from the previous lines. Two אמוראים disagree about the starting point for counting the days before מתן תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא counts from the day the Jews arrived and camped at סיני. רב אחא בר יעקב counts from the day they left רפידים, which in his view was that same Sunday, since they set out and arrived on one day. The underlying question is whether the Jews were allowed to travel out of רפידים on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: from their camping (arrival at Sinai)
from their journey (departure from Refidim)
the camp the Jews traveled from to reach Sinai

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רבא's name here. His statement began on the previous amud, and only its last word, 'לחנייתן', appears here.

phrases.english: [Rava said: the sixth day] from their encampment.
phrases.notes: Ends רבא's statement, which began earlier.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
From their journey.
phrases.notes: Counted from leaving רפידים, which in his view was the same day they arrived.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: לְמַסָּעָן

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא counts from the camping at Sinai. רב אחא בר יעקב counts from the journey out of Refidim.

steps.title: The root of the dispute: what was commanded at מרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the dispute depends on the שבת laws given at מרה, which it shows from a פסוק and from רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about the שבת given at מרה. As it is written: 'As ה׳ your God commanded you.' And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: 'As He commanded you' means at מרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its explanation of the dispute. It first proves that the Jews were already commanded about שבת at מרה, before Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second לוחות, the פסוק about שבת says 'as ה׳ commanded you.' That points back to an earlier command, and רב says it was given at מרה. So before Sinai the Jews already had some שבת laws, and the next step asks which ones.

keyTerms.meaning: they disagree
Marah, the stop where some מצוות were given before Sinai
as He commanded you

phrases.english: And they disagree about the Shabbat of Marah.
As it is written: "As the Lord your God commanded you,"
phrases.notes: דברים 5:11, the fourth commandment in the second לוחות.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
"As He commanded you" means at Marah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining why רבא and רב אחא בר יעקב disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Jews received a שבת command at מרה, before מתן תורה.

steps.title: שבת only, or תחומין too
steps.stepSummary: One view: at מרה they were commanded about שבת but not about תחומין. The other view: they were commanded about תחומין too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: they were commanded about שבת but not about the boundaries. The other master holds: they were commanded about the boundaries too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the dispute. The two אמוראים disagree about whether the מרה commands included the limits on walking far on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there was no command about תחומין yet, the Jews could leave רפידים on שבת, so counting from the journey works. That is רב אחא בר יעקב's view. If תחומין was already in force, they could not travel on שבת, so the count starts from the camping on Sunday. That is רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: they were commanded
Shabbat boundaries, the limit on how far one may walk outside a town on שבת
one master holds

steps.whatToRemember: The רפידים dispute rests on one question: were תחומין part of the מרה commands or not?

phrases.english: One master holds: they were commanded about Shabbat,
but they were not commanded about the boundaries.
And the other master holds: they were also commanded about the boundaries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation begun in Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute depends on whether תחומין was commanded at מרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the dates of יציאת מצרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing the dates in ניסן of the year the Jews left Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: in ניסן, when the Jews left Egypt, they slaughtered their קרבן פסח on the 14th, left on the 15th, and in the evening the firstborn were struck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to רבנן by quoting a ברייתא with Exodus dates. The calculation that makes it a challenge comes in Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא returns to the main question: was ראש חודש סיון a Sunday or a Monday? The dates in this ברייתא, together with the day of the week given later, will let us work out the calendar.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a source)
their Pesach offerings
the firstborn were struck

phrases.english: Come and hear:
In the Nisan in which Israel left Egypt,
on the fourteenth they slaughtered their Paschal lambs,
and on the fifteenth they left,
and in the evening the firstborn were struck.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִיסָן שֶׁבּוֹ יָצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the Refidim side point and back to the main calendar dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבנן's view that ראש חודש סיון was on Monday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup only. The ברייתא's dates will produce a Sunday ראש חודש.

steps.title: Struck in the evening, after they left?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how could the firstborn be struck in the evening after the Jews had already left?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think it was in the evening?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question the ברייתא's wording. The plague of the firstborn came before the Jews left, not after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jews left Egypt because of the plague of the firstborn. So the plague cannot have come on the evening after the 15th. The wording needs to be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: can it enter your mind? (meaning: that can't be right)

phrases.english: Does it enter your mind that it was in the evening?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the plague come after the Jews left?

steps.title: Correction: the evening before
steps.stepSummary: The answer: read it as 'the evening before.' The firstborn were struck on the night of the 15th, before the Jews left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the firstborn were struck on the evening before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא. The plague came on the night before the Jews left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jewish day starts at night. So the night of the 15th comes before the daytime of the 15th, when the Jews went out. This fix leaves the dates in place for the calculation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: from the evening before

phrases.english: Rather: the firstborn were struck on the evening before,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Read it as 'the evening before': the plague came on the night of the 15th.

steps.title: The calendar puts ראש חודש סיון on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: The 15th of ניסן was a Thursday. With ניסן full and אייר short, ראש חודש סיון was a Sunday, which is hard for רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that day was a Thursday. Since the 15th of ניסן was a Thursday, ראש חודש אייר was שבת and ראש חודש סיון was Sunday. This is difficult for רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us the 15th of ניסן was a Thursday. The גמרא counts forward and finds that ראש חודש סיון was a Sunday, so it challenges רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 15th was a Thursday, the 1st of ניסן was also a Thursday. A usual 30-day ניסן puts the 1st of אייר on שבת, and a usual 29-day אייר puts the 1st of סיון on Sunday. Then the 6th of סיון is a Friday, but רבנן say the תורה was given on שבת the 6th.

keyTerms.meaning: the fifth day of the week (Thursday)
the start of the month (ראש חודש)
it is difficult

phrases.english: And that day was the fifth day of the week.
Since the fifteenth of Nisan was a Thursday,
the New Moon of Iyyar was on Shabbat,
and the New Moon of Sivan was on Sunday,
This is difficult for the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the corrected ברייתא to work out the calendar.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבנן: ראש חודש סיון was Monday, and the תורה was given on the 6th.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting forward from Thursday the 15th of ניסן, with ניסן full and אייר short, ראש חודש סיון lands on Sunday.
steps.confusionAlert: Months were 29 or 30 days, depending on when בית דין declared the new month. The challenge only works if we assume ניסן had 30 days and אייר had 29.

steps.title: That year אייר was made 30 days
steps.stepSummary: רבנן answer that אייר was given an extra day that year, so ראש חודש סיון was Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן can tell you: that year, אייר was lengthened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבנן. It says the assumption that אייר had 29 days is not certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אייר had 30 days, ראש חודש סיון moves from Sunday to Monday. Then the 6th of סיון is שבת, just as רבנן say.

keyTerms.meaning: they could say to you
they lengthened it (added a day to the month)

phrases.english: The Rabbis could say to you:
The Iyyar of that year was made a full month (thirty days).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenge's assumption about the length of the month.
steps.terutzMaskana: אייר had 30 days, so ראש חודש סיון was Monday.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: אייר was not lengthened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, introduced as proof that אייר was not lengthened. It repeats the same dates and the same correction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear that they did not lengthen it: in ניסן, when the Jews left Egypt, they slaughtered their קרבן פסח on the 14th, left on the 15th, and in the evening the firstborn were struck. Can you think it was the evening? Rather, say the evening before. And that day was a Thursday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to the answer in Step 8. It quotes a ברייתא that repeats the earlier text and will go on to state the length of each month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the earlier one word for word, including the 'evening' correction. Its new purpose is to lead into the month lengths it states in Step 10. The opening words 'דלא עברוה' already tell us the goal is to undo the answer in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: that they did not lengthen it
say (read it as)

phrases.english: Come and hear that they did not lengthen it:

on the fifteenth they left,

Does it enter your mind that it was in the evening?!
Rather, say: the firstborn were struck on the evening before.
And that day was the fifth day of the week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a challenge to the answer in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that אייר was lengthened that year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup. The ברייתא will go on to say directly that אייר was short.

steps.title: ניסן full, אייר short: difficult for רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that ניסן was full and אייר was short, so ראש חודש סיון was a Sunday. The challenge to רבנן returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: ניסן was full, and ראש חודש אייר fell on שבת. אייר was short, and ראש חודש סיון fell on Sunday. This is difficult for רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא itself gives the month lengths. That blocks the answer that אייר had 30 days, and the challenge to רבנן comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the month lengths were the גמרא's assumption. Here they are written in the ברייתא, so רבנן can no longer claim an extra day in אייר.

keyTerms.meaning: was full (30 days)
was short (29 days)
it happened to fall

phrases.english: Nisan was full,

Iyyar was lacking,

This is difficult for the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: הִשְׁלִים נִיסָן וְאֵירַע אִיָּיר לִהְיוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge set up in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבנן, and the answer in Step 8 that אייר was lengthened.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא itself says אייר had 29 days, so ראש חודש סיון was Sunday and not Monday.

steps.title: This ברייתא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, who holds that ראש חודש סיון was a Sunday. So it is no challenge to רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying who the ברייתא follows. It reflects רבי יוסי's view, and רבנן disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says the תורה was given on the 7th of סיון with ראש חודש on Sunday, which fits this ברייתא exactly. A ברייתא that follows the other side of the dispute does not prove רבנן wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: whose view is this?
the תנא who holds the תורה was given on the 7th of סיון

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges to רבנן are answered. The first fails because אייר may have been lengthened. The second ברייתא, which says אייר was short, follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Yosei's.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the source to the other side of the dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is accepted by everyone and so disproves רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, so רבנן are not challenged.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבנן's view, that ראש חודש סיון was Monday and the תורה was given on the 6th, still stands.

steps.title: רב פפא shows from the מן story that the 15th of אייר was שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a new proof from פסוקים: בני ישראל arrived at מדבר סין on the 15th of the second month, and that day was שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Come and hear. The פסוק says, "They traveled from Elim, and the whole congregation of Israel came... on the fifteenth day of the second month." That day was שבת. We know this because it says, "In the morning you will see the glory of ה׳," and it also says, "Six days you shall gather it."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is setting up a new challenge. First he proves from פסוקים that the 15th of אייר was שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the 15th of אייר the people complained. The next morning (the 16th) the מן began to fall, and they gathered it for six days before the first שבת. So the 16th was Sunday, which means the 15th was שבת.

The second month, counting from ניסן, which is אייר

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup only. The פסוקים prove that 15 אייר was שבת, which step 13 turns into a Sunday ראש חודש סיון.

steps.title: So ראש חודש סיון was Sunday, which is hard for רבנן
steps.stepSummary: If the 15th of אייר was שבת, then ראש חודש סיון was Sunday. This contradicts רבנן, who say Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the 15th of אייר was שבת, ראש חודש סיון was Sunday. That is a difficulty for רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the date from the last step to challenge רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 15th was שבת, then the 22nd and 29th were also שבת. A normal אייר has 29 days, so the next day, ראש חודש סיון, was Sunday. רבנן hold it was Monday.

steps.title: רבנן answer that אייר was lengthened that year
steps.stepSummary: רבנן reply that אייר had 30 days that year, so ראש חודש סיון was Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן can say to you: That year, they added a day to אייר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבנן answer the challenge the same way they did in step 8. They say אייר was a full month that year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 30 days in אייר, the 30th was Sunday, and ראש חודש סיון moves to Monday. This fits רבנן's view.

steps.terutzMaskana: That year אייר had 30 days, so סיון began on Monday, as רבנן say.

steps.title: רב חביבי: the משכן was set up on a Sunday, ראש חודש ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבי brings a ברייתא showing that the day the משכן was set up, ראש חודש ניסן of the second year, was a Sunday. That day had "ten crowns."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבי from מחוזנא said to רב אשי: Come and hear. The פסוק says, "In the first month of the second year, on the first of the month, the משכן was set up." A ברייתא taught: That day received ten crowns. It was first for the days of creation (a Sunday), first for the offerings of the נשיאים, first for כהונה, first for the עבודה, first for fire coming down, first for eating קדשים, first for the שכינה resting, first for blessing Israel, first for forbidding במות, and first of the months.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבי is setting up another challenge. He first proves that ראש חודש ניסן in the second year was a Sunday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key crown is "first for the days of creation," which means the day was a Sunday. The other crowns praise the day but are not needed for the calendar argument.

phrases.aramaic: רִאשׁוֹן לִירִידַת הָאֵשׁ; רִאשׁוֹן לַאֲכִילַת קָדָשִׁים;
phrases.english: first for the descent of fire; first for eating holy offerings;

phrases.aramaic: רִאשׁוֹן לִשְׁכּוֹן שְׁכִינָה; רִאשׁוֹן לְבָרֵךְ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל;
phrases.english: first for the Divine Presence to rest; first for blessing Israel;
first for the prohibition of private altars; first of the months.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲבִיבִי מָחוֹזְנָאָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא's proof was answered, a new proof begins from a different source.
steps.raayaObject: That ראש חודש ניסן in the second year was a Sunday
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the ten crowns: "first of the days of creation"
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רבי יוסי (ראש חודש סיון was Sunday) and רבנן (it was Monday)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup only. The ברייתא shows that ראש חודש ניסן of the second year was Sunday. Steps 16–18 count back a year and land ראש חודש סיון of the Exodus year on שבת.

steps.title: So the year before, ראש חודש ניסן was a Wednesday
steps.stepSummary: If ראש חודש ניסן of the second year was Sunday, then in the year of יציאת מצרים it was Wednesday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since ראש חודש ניסן this year was Sunday, last year it was on the fourth day of the week (Wednesday).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counts backward one year from the Sunday it just proved. This gives the weekday of ראש חודש ניסן in the year they left מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal lunar year has 354 days, which is 50 full weeks plus 4 days. So each date moves 4 weekdays forward each year. Going back 4 days from Sunday gives Wednesday.

keyTerms.meaning: Last year
On the fourth day of the week, Wednesday

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּרֵישׁ יַרְחָא דְנִיסָן דְּהָא שַׁתָּא חַד בְּשַׁבָּא —
phrases.english: And since Rosh Chodesh Nisan of this year was on Sunday —
last year it was on Wednesday.
phrases.notes: Count back four weekdays: Sunday → Wednesday.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרֵישׁ יַרְחָא דְנִיסָן דְּהָא שַׁתָּא חַד בְּשַׁבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It applies calendar math to the Sunday proved in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the year of יציאת מצרים, ראש חודש ניסן was on Wednesday.

steps.title: The source: a year moves dates by four weekdays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of אחרים says that from one שבועות to the next, and from one ראש השנה to the next, the weekday moves by 4 days, or 5 in a leap year.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say, Between one עצרת and the next, and between one ראש השנה and the next, there are only four days of difference. If it was a leap year, there are five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the four-day rule it used in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes a fixed pattern: six months of 30 days and six of 29, for 354 days a year. That leaves exactly 4 extra days beyond whole weeks. A leap year, which adds a month, shifts by 5.

keyTerms.meaning: "Others": a תנא quoted by this name
Assembly: a name for שבועות
A leap year, with an extra month

steps.confusionAlert: "Four days" does not mean the holidays are four days apart. It means the weekday moves forward by four. For example, if שבועות was Sunday this year, next year it is Thursday.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Acherim say:
Between one Atzeret (Shavuot) and the next

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בֵּין רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: and between one Rosh HaShana and the next
there is a difference of only four days of the week,
and if it was a leap year — five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the source for step 16's calculation.
steps.raayaObject: That the weekday moves 4 days from one year to the next

steps.title: Then ראש חודש סיון was שבת, which is hard for everyone
steps.stepSummary: With ראש חודש ניסן on Wednesday, ראש חודש אייר falls on Friday and ראש חודש סיון on שבת. That fits neither רבי יוסי (Sunday) nor רבנן (Monday).
steps.simpleTranslation: So ראש חודש אייר was ערב שבת, and ראש חודש סיון was שבת. This is a difficulty for both רבי יוסי and רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the calculation and challenges both opinions at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניסן has 30 days, so starting Wednesday, אייר begins on Friday. אייר has 29 days, so סיון begins on שבת. Both opinions said ראש חודש סיון came after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The eve of שבת, Friday
Both for רבי יוסי and for רבנן

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה לֵיהּ רֵישׁ יַרְחָא דְאִיָּיר מַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא,
phrases.english: So Rosh Chodesh Iyar was on Friday,
phrases.notes: Wednesday plus 30 days of ניסן gives Friday.

phrases.english: and Rosh Chodesh Sivan was on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Friday plus 29 days of אייר gives שבת.

phrases.aramaic: קַשְׁיָא בֵּין לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן!
phrases.english: this is difficult both for Rabbi Yosei and for the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא בֵּין לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It completes the calculation begun in steps 15 to 17 and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רבי יוסי (ראש חודש סיון was Sunday) and רבנן (it was Monday)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the fixed 4-day pattern, ראש חודש סיון of the Exodus year falls on שבת, which fits neither view.

steps.title: For רבי יוסי: that year had seven short months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer. According to רבי יוסי, the year of יציאת מצרים had seven 29-day months, so the 4-day rule of אחרים does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יוסי, they made seven months short that year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer by rejecting the fixed pattern of אחרים. It begins with רבי יוסי, and the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If seven months were short instead of six, the year had 353 days, so dates moved only 3 weekdays. Counting back from Sunday, ראש חודש ניסן of the Exodus year was Thursday, which fits the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven short months of 29 days each
They made: the months were set that way

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yosei, they made seven short months,
phrases.notes: This means 353 days, so dates shift by 3 weekdays, not 4. The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins answering the double challenge of step 18, starting with רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the assumed fixed month pattern of אחרים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every year has exactly six full and six short months, so dates shift 4 weekdays.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, that year had seven short months, so the shift was smaller. This removes the conflict, and the answer for רבנן follows.
